newsitem.title: FINLAND: Pohjola sees no harm from govt ruling.
newsitem.headline: Pohjola sees no harm from govt ruling.

text.p: Finnish insurance company Pohjola said on Wednesday a government rejection of its proposal to become a holding company would not hamper the overall plan to absorb mutual Suomi life insurance portfolio.

"This has no impact on the structure ... it does not harm the restructuting" Pohjola CEO Iiro Viinanen told a news conference when asked whether the government's ruling would affect Pohjola group's planned restructuring.
Pohjola said earlier that the ministry of social affairs and health had not approved its plan to become a holding company.

On January 23, Pohjola announced plans to become a holding company with two main subsidiaries -- the current non-life insurance business and the life-insurance business Salama which is now part of associated Suomi.
Viinanen said that the holding company structure would have been "clearer" with Pohjola as an insurance company, but otherwise there were no big differences between the two plans.
Pohjola's new group structure would take effect by July 1 as planned, Viinanen said. -- Ilkka Virtanen, Helsinki newsroom +358-9-6805 0248
